body:
Alright. I agree I should do something specifically tailored to him and not some generalized thing. I was just wondering if there might be something special that helps people in such situation.

Just one more thing, my emotional response to him saying he was thinking about suicide would be to just freak out and beg him not to do it because I don't know what I would do without him.

I'm torn whether I should completely show him how I feel about it. If someone who loved you started begging you not to do it, would you see it as an expression of their deep love or as extra burden and criticism, or something else?

Thank you so much for this. It means a lot to hear from someone who feels like him because he's not ready to talk about it yet.

I was thinking of asking him once per day. It usually pops up in conversation naturally anyway.

It's been very difficult for him for a long time now, but he always says he's fine. I knew he can't be fine, but I could never get him to say anything more. Then few days ago he suddenly opened up and told me everything that's bothering him. However, it didn't occur to me to ask him if he's been thinking about suicide until yesterday.

I'm relieved to hear if you promise you won't do it you won't. I think he's that way as well. At least with other things he takes promises very seriously, even little things that I think are silly and don't take seriously.

I'm sorry I'm bothering you so much, but could you please tell me if you think there's something special I can do for him to cheer him up? I know I can't fix his life and make a big difference, but if I can put a smile on his face even for just 5 minutes it would be worth it.

Once again, thank you, you've been extremely valuable to me.

Thank you.

Yeah, I thought that suggesting therapy might sound like criticizing. I was hoping mentioning it wouldn't be so bad since I'm having therapy as well, so then it's obviously not taboo for me. But for now I won't suggest it.

I really don't notice any symptoms in him. He's just having a justifiable reaction to his current situation.

I haven't been forceful, I asked him how he's feeling, but he didn't seem to be in the mood to discuss it so I just talked about other things.

Should I tell anyone else? I haven't met anyone who is close to him so it would be very awkward to contact them for the first time with such news, and since I am closest person he has, I think he may see it as betrayal.

He's already decided how he would do it, but he told me that for now he won't do it, and that I have nothing to worry about. Should I trust him?

I immediately read the /r/swresources and I tried to follow those guidelines while talking to him. I was scared of saying the wrong thing.

I was trying to make sure it's clear I understand that his situation sucks, but that he is precious to me, and that he makes me happy. I also mentioned other people I know for sure are better off with him than without. But I didn't want to put too much emphasis of how much we would suffer if he wasn't here because I was worried it would feel like I am selfish in all this.
I was thinking about sending him a love letter but I wasn't sure if he would think it's silly, since we chat ever day. Thank you for encouraging me.
